task: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Spirit Airlines

nimble.claim: Spirit Airlines (Spirit Aviation Holdings) is private, formerly NYSE: SAVE; ownership passed to former creditors (bondholders) on emerging from first Chapter 11 on 2025-03-12 via exchange of ~$795M funded debt for equity plus a $296.1M equity rights offering (7,770,054 shares issued); no PE sponsor or founder owner.
Spirit Airlines total operating revenues were $958.5M in Q3 2025 (three months ended 2025-09-30, Successor period).
Spirit Airlines total operating expenses were $1,093.4M in Q3 2025, exceeding revenue by about $135M.
Spirit Airlines had $646.6M of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash as of 2025-09-30.
Spirit Airlines had $408M unrestricted cash as of 2025-06-30, with its $275M revolver fully drawn (per Moody's via Reuters).
Spirit Airlines had about $2.4B of long-term debt (most due 2030) at its second Chapter 11 filing in August 2025.
Spirit Airlines had negative free cash flow of about $1B as of end of Q2 2025.
Spirit Airlines combined FY2025 net loss was about $2.7B (predecessor plus successor, including $2.1B reorganization items).
Spirit Airlines combined FY2025 total revenue was about $3.7B.
Spirit Airlines had $864.3M of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit Airlines January 2026 revenue was $250.3M, with operating loss of $42.0M (operating margin -17%).
Spirit Airlines January 2026 net loss was $125.1M, including $83.1M of other/reorganization expenses.
Spirit Airlines had adjusted cash and restricted cash of $822M at end of January 2026, versus $867M at end-December 2025.
Spirit Airlines had $3.6B total outstanding debt at its November 2024 Chapter 11 petition, with 21,000 employees/contractors and a 213-aircraft A320 fleet (51 owned).

Bankruptcy Court approved on 2025-10-31 a Spirit Airlines 2025 DIP Facility of up to $1.2B, including a roll-up of pre-petition secured notes up to $750M; the earlier $300M 2024 DIP was repaid at first emergence.
Spirit Airlines' post-bankruptcy plan (published 2026-03-15) projected a 2026 net loss of $111M and a 2027 net profit of $55M on $2.6B revenue; the plan was overtaken by the May 2026 shutdown.
Spirit Airlines filed Chapter 11 on 2024-11-18 in SDNY with $3.6B total debt, after the JetBlue merger was blocked and with $2.5B+ cumulative losses since 2020.
Spirit Airlines launched a $350M equity rights offering ($14.00/share) on 2024-12-30; it closed at emergence with $296,107,812 consideration (7,770,054 shares and 13,380,504 warrants).

Spirit Airlines emerged from first Chapter 11 on 2025-03-12, equitizing about $795M of funded debt; repaid the $300M 2024 DIP and $300M revolver; entered a new $275M exit revolver maturing 2026, reduced to $250M on 2026-09-30.

On 2025-08-15 Spirit Airlines transferred an additional $50M cash to a pledged account with its credit-card processor (USB) and agreed to holdbacks of up to $3M/day until fully collateralized, in exchange for extending the processing agreement to 2027-12-31.
On 2025-08-21 Spirit Airlines warned it might not survive a year without significantly more cash and drew the entire $275M revolver, disclosing going-concern risk with Q2 2025 results.
Spirit Airlines filed its second Chapter 11 on 2025-08-29 (Case No. 25-11897, SDNY) with $2.4B long-term debt and $1B negative FCF at Q2 2025; lessor AerCap had terminated aircraft leases.

On 2025-10-31 the Bankruptcy Court approved a final order for Spirit Airlines' multi-draw senior secured super-priority priming DIP facility of up to $1.2B, including roll-up of pre-petition secured notes up to $750M.

On 2026-03-13 Spirit Airlines filed a plan of reorganization, disclosure statement and RSA with consenting DIP lenders; it later pivoted to wind-down, seeking to auction LaGuardia slots, corporate campus, loyalty program and equipment, and to sell/abandon 28 owned aircraft and 18 spare engines.

Spirit Airlines ceased all flight operations on 2026-05-02 after bailout talks (~$500M proposal with the Trump administration) collapsed, blaming sharply higher fuel costs from the 2026 Iran war; began orderly wind-down and liquidation.

On 2026-05-05 Judge Sean H. Lane approved Spirit Airlines' wind-down procedures and granted aircraft lease rejection and sale motions; the U.S. Trustee's suggestion to convert to Chapter 7 was not pressed.
Spirit Airlines claims bar dates: general proofs of claim due 2026-01-27, governmental units 2026-02-25, pre-wind-down administrative expense claims 2026-07-27.

S&P downgraded Spirit Airlines to 'CCC' from 'CCC+' on 2024-06-05, outlook negative, citing 2025 maturities ($1.1B loyalty bonds due Sep 2025, $500M convertibles 2026), less than adequate liquidity, and likely distressed exchange within 12 months.
Fitch downgraded Spirit Airlines to 'CCC-' from 'CCC+' on 2025-08-18, citing operational losses, deteriorating liquidity and default risk.
Fitch downgraded Spirit's loyalty-program debt to 'CCC-' from 'B-' on 2025-08-18, with recovery rating RR4 from RR3.
Moody's downgraded Spirit Airlines two notches to Caa3 on 2025-08-22, citing higher than expected cash burn; forecast over $500M cash burn in 2025; revolver matures March 2028.
Spirit Airlines' Moody's rating fell from B2 (2023) to Caa3 (2025); S&P projected a $600M free cash flow deficit for 2025, with negative outlooks.

Spirit Airlines CEO Ted Christie exited on 2025-04-07 weeks after emergence from first bankruptcy, and CCO Matt Klein stepped down; an office of the president ran the company until Dave Davis was named CEO.
Spirit Airlines disclosed 'substantial doubt' about going-concern ability with Q2 2025 results, repeated in its Q3 2025 Form 10-Q.

Spirit Airlines discontinued service in 11 U.S. cities from October 2025, furloughed ~270 pilots from Nov 1, downgraded 140 captains, and confirmed 1,800 flight-attendant furloughs (nearly one-third of cabin crew) by Dec 1, 2025.
Spirit Airlines cut about 150 corporate/market jobs and exited several markets on 2025-11-05.
An Examiner was appointed in Spirit Airlines' Chapter 11 case (SDNY) in October 2025.
By 2026-04-15 Spirit Airlines was reported at risk of imminent liquidation amid jet-fuel price surge; by April 18 it sought a federal bailout and the administration considered a controlling stake.

Spirit Airlines shut down on 2026-05-02; employee health insurance ended that day; Florida WARN notices showed more than 4,850 layoffs (2,529 FLL, 551 Dania Beach, 181 MIA, 796 MCO plus 796 MCO inflight/ops center).
Spirit Airlines' fleet shrank from 214 aircraft pre-bankruptcy toward a planned 76 by mid-August 2026, with international routes slashed.
Aircraft lessor AerCap terminated Spirit Airlines aircraft leases ahead of the second Chapter 11, and Spirit later sought court approval to reject remaining aircraft leases.

Broward County (FLL operator) asserted liens on Spirit Airlines aircraft for postpetition administrative claims on 2026-05-05; trade counterparties, airports, lessors and insurers forced modifications to the wind-down order.

exa.claim: Spirit Airlines, LLC is a wholly owned operating subsidiary of Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc.; the March 2025 reorganization installed the holding company as parent and converted former Spirit Airlines, Inc. into an LLC (status as of 2026-05-02).

Spirit Airlines, LLC held cash of $231,834,781 as of 2026-08-31 per its August monthly operating report (filed 2026-09-22, docket 1632), as transcribed by a secondary source; bankruptcy-report cash, not verified unrestricted liquidity.

Spirit Airlines, LLC is the borrower under the interim DIP order dated 2025-08-29 in its second Chapter 11 proceeding (case 25-11897, SDNY, jointly administered), with Spirit Aviation Holdings and affiliates as guarantors.
Spirit's DIP financing included a $200 million new-money draw on 2025-10-14.
Spirit's DIP financing included a $50 million new-money draw on 2025-11-07.
Spirit's DIP financing included a $100 million additional new-money draw on 2025-12-15.

On 2026-05-02 Spirit announced immediate wind-down and cancellation of all flights, stating no additional funding was available; CEO Dave Davis said continuing required hundreds of millions of dollars of liquidity Spirit could not procure, so the proposed March bondholder restructuring did not preserve an operating airline.
As of 2026-10-14 Spirit Airlines' liquidation was ongoing, with a simulator sale, continued aircraft-sale disputes, and the proposed data sale hearing adjourned to 2026-11-06.
Fitch downgraded Spirit Airlines, LLC to D on 2025-09-04.
On 2026-05-06 Fitch affirmed Spirit Airlines, LLC at D and withdrew its long-term issuer default rating (WD) the same day; no active outlook.

Spirit Airlines cancelled all flights on 2026-05-02 and began immediate wind-down after being unable to obtain sufficient liquidity; the company attributed the failed turnaround to materially higher oil prices and other business pressures.
CNBC reported on 2026-05-04 that approximately 17,000 direct and indirect Spirit workers lost jobs; CEO Dave Davis remained with about 130 other employees to oversee closure.
Spirit Aviation Holdings' (parent) 2025 Form 10-K, dated 2026-03-16, stated substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern and warned liquidation could be required.

NBC reported on 2026-05-14 a proposed employee class action in Spirit Airlines' bankruptcy court alleging layoffs without required WARN notice and seeking unpaid wages and benefits; some former employees reported missing final paychecks (allegations, not adjudicated).

Spirit Airlines said on 2026-05-02 that flights bought directly by credit/debit card would be automatically refunded, while compensation for vouchers, credits and Free Spirit points would be determined later through bankruptcy.

parallel.claim: Spirit Airlines, LLC is a Chapter 11 debtor; as of 2026-10-20 the credit risk call is high.

Spirit Airlines, LLC is a wholly owned subsidiary of Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc., a public-reporting holding company; the March 12, 2025 reorganization made the airline an LLC beneath that parent, with new parent shares and warrants issued to certain creditors (as of 2025-12-31).

On 2026-05-02 Spirit Airlines started an immediate orderly wind-down and cancelled all flights, stating additional funding was unavailable and the business required additional liquidity it could not procure.
Spirit Airlines, LLC's July 2026 monthly operating report showed 76 full-time employees as of August 1, 2026, versus 9,229 as of September 30, 2025.
On 2026-05-06 Fitch affirmed Spirit Airlines, LLC's Long-Term Issuer Default Rating at D, then withdrew the issuer rating following the decision to cease operations and enter bankruptcy liquidation.
On 2026-05-21 S&P Global Ratings withdrew all ratings on Spirit Airlines LLC, including its EETC ratings, because of insufficient information.

Spirit Airlines, LLC reported ending cash/restricted cash of $266,849,907 as of 2026-07-31 in its unaudited monthly operating report; this reflects pooled debtor bank accounts, excludes intercompany cash flows, and is not unrestricted or freely available liquidity.

On 2026-05-02 Spirit Airlines announced automatic refunds for flights bought directly with credit or debit cards, while compensation for bookings paid with vouchers, credits or Free Spirit points would be determined later through the bankruptcy process.
Spirit Airlines told Reuters on 2026-05-03 that most customers who paid by credit or debit card had been refunded by the evening of May 2, with a small percentage still processing.

Spirit Airlines, LLC filed for Chapter 11 protection on 2025-08-29 in the Southern District of New York (case 25-11896), jointly administered with Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. and affiliates under lead case 25-11897.

On 2025-10-14 Spirit Airlines, LLC, as borrower, entered a debtor-in-possession credit agreement providing for up to $475 million of aggregate term loans, with certain subsidiaries as guarantors, subject to funding conditions.

On 2025-12-15 Spirit announced an amendment to its DIP credit agreement for a $100 million incremental funding round, of which $50 million (less original issue discount) was immediately usable and the remainder depended on progress toward a standalone reorganization or strategic transaction.
On 2026-05-02 Spirit Airlines could not obtain additional financing and began winding down operations, saying sustaining the business required liquidity it did not have and could not procure.

firecrawl.claim: Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. reported operating revenue of $3,796,747,000 for FY2025 (year ended 2025-12-31, combined predecessor and successor periods).
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. reported a successor-period operating loss of $481,511,000 for 2025-03-13 to 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. reported a predecessor-period operating loss of $287,199,000 for 2025-01-01 to 2025-03-12.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. had cash and cash equivalents (unrestricted) of $272,959,000 as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. reported long-term debt before current maturities and unamortized discounts of $1,258.7 million as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. had $1,609.4 million of debt classified within liabilities subject to compromise as of 2025-12-31.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. fully drew its $275 million exit revolving credit facility on 2025-08-21 to fund operations and credit-card collateral requirements.
S&P Global Ratings downgraded Spirit Airlines LLC's issuer credit rating to D from CCC on 2025-09-02 after the 2025 Chapter 11 filing.
Fitch downgraded Spirit Airlines' Long-Term Issuer Default Rating to D from CCC- on 2025-09-04 after the second Chapter 11 filing, and downgraded related senior secured debt to C/RR4.

Moody's downgraded Spirit Airlines LLC's corporate family rating to Caa3 from Caa1 on 2025-08-22, with probability of default rating Caa3-PD from Caa1-PD, speculative-grade liquidity rating SGL-4 from SGL-3, and outlook negative from stable.

Spirit emerged from its first Chapter 11 case on 2025-03-12 after about $795 million of funded debt was equitized, with a $350 million equity investment, $840 million of exit secured notes due 2030 and a $275 million exit revolving facility.

Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. and five affiliates filed voluntary Chapter 11 petitions in the Southern District of New York (Case No. 25-11897) on 2025-08-29, its second Chapter 11 filing in less than a year.

From the 2025-08-29 petition date, Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. ceased making principal and interest payments and ceased accruing interest on long-term debt reclassified as liabilities subject to compromise.
The Bankruptcy Court approved on 2025-10-31 a super-priority DIP facility for Spirit of up to $1.2 billion, including up to $475 million new-money loans and up to $750 million roll-up DIP loans.
Spirit drew new-money DIP loans of $200 million on 2025-10-14, $50 million on 2025-11-07 and $100 million on 2025-12-15.

On 2025-12-15 Spirit amended the DIP credit agreement and drew the full $100 million third new-money draw; $50 million net of OID was immediately available and $50 million had to remain encumbered pending restructuring or exit-financing progress.

On 2026-05-02 Spirit began an orderly wind-down with all flights cancelled, stating no additional funding was available and that it could not procure the hundreds of millions of additional liquidity needed.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. reported $124.4 million of accounts payable within liabilities subject to compromise as of 2025-12-31, pre-petition obligations subject to the automatic stay.

On 2026-05-02 Spirit said card-ticket refunds would be processed to the original payment method, while vouchers, credits and Free Spirit points would be addressed later through the bankruptcy process, and customer service was no longer available.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. management stated that substantial doubt existed about its ability to continue as a going concern within one year of filing the 2025 Form 10-K.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc.'s 2025 Form 10-K reported a 17.4% reduction in the pilot and flight-attendant workforce from headcount rationalization and restructuring.
Spirit attributed its 2026-05-02 shutdown to a material rise in oil prices, other business pressures and the absence of additional funding.

Reuters reported on 2026-05-04 that Spirit planned to retain about 150 employees during the wind-down and cut to about 40 after three months; CFO Fred Comer said there was no viable path to continued operations.

As of 2026-04-15, Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc.'s largest disclosed 5% holders were PIMCO (9.5%), Arena Capital Advisors (9.1%), AllianceBernstein (8.4%), Cyrus Capital (7.6%), Ares Management (7.0%), M&G (6.5%) and Citadel (5.7%).
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. changed its name from Spirit Airlines, Inc. on 2025-03-13.
After the 2026-05-02 wind-down, Spirit's remaining assets are controlled by the bankruptcy estate and court-supervised process, and common-stock holders were told to expect a complete loss.
